purpose: Training set for the leaf model's thermal calibration (leaf-v1). Per-year observed peak fall-color date at a 3,300 ft reference elevation in the Boone-to-Grandfather corridor, 2008-2025, paired with the September mean daily temperature published alongside it.

provenance.document: Fall Color Studies: 'Are There Any Trends in the Timing of Peak Fall Leaf Color' (.docx), linked from the site's Fall Color Studies page
provenance.extraction_method: The document's per-year values are published as charts, not tables. Each year's peak day and September mean was read off the charts and CROSS-VALIDATED across three independent figures in the same document: the peak-day-vs-year scatter, the September-mean-by-year bar chart, and the peak-day-vs-September-temperature scatter. All 17 graded pairs agree across all three figures, and the pairs reproduce the document's own stated regression (slope 1.9015, intercept -106.42, R2 0.62) to three decimal places -- see scripts/fit_leaf_v1.py's 'published series' line. Values are therefore digitized, not transcribed, and carry roughly +-0.1 degF / +-0 days of reading error.
provenance.owner_ruling: David, 2026-09-03/09-04: this record may be used to TRAIN the model. Facts (dates, temperatures, elevations) are ingestable; prose is not. Nothing user-facing cites the source -- see docs/leaf-model.md's provenance line and the registry's internal_only flag.

reference.geography: Boone to Grandfather Mountain corridor, western North Carolina
reference.peak_definition: The observer's own weekly declaration of landscape-scale peak color (all species together, not species-specific). The charted value is the midpoint of the week declared peak, so each date carries roughly +-3 days of intrinsic resolution.
reference.temperature_definition: Mean of daily high and low, averaged over the full calendar month of September, from the observer's own station record -- NOT from the Open-Meteo archive the model uses. scripts/fit_leaf_v1.py cross-checks the two series.

notes: 2024 has a September mean but NO observed peak: the record excludes it because of Hurricane Helene.
The published long-term September mean is 64.7 degF over these 18 years, with a stated range of 62.1 (2012) to 69.4 (2018). Both endpoints are reproduced below.

Drought and precipitation were tested against peak timing in the same document -- monthly totals, seasonal totals, cumulative amounts, and the Palmer Drought Index -- and none showed a significant relationship. Recorded in docs/leaf-model.md as a tested exclusion; no precipitation term belongs in the date model.

years.excluded_reason: Hurricane Helene; the source excludes 2024 from its peak-timing record.
